name: Seafoam Green
lede: Seafoam Green is a pale yellow-beige that Maerz and Paul trace to 1892, sharing a name but no real kinship with the bright green Seafoam.

sections.title: Pale, beige, and misleadingly named
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 plates give this pale yellow-beige at hue 27′′, tone f, on plate XXXI, and the Inter-Society Color Council's 1955 census files it in block 121 as a pale yellow, Munsell 5.9Y 8.9/2.6 [1]. Maerz and Paul trace the name itself to 1892 [1].

Despite sharing a name with the bright green [[seafoam]], Seafoam Green sits nowhere near it in hue: its nearest library match shares its exact hex, [[lemon-meringue]], with [[marguerite-yellow]] and [[pale-chalcedony-yellow]] both within 3 units [1]. ColorHub's broader palette map also places it near [[beige]], about 4.2 units off [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds Seafoam Green in 584 of 23,781 paintings, about 2.5 percent, almost always as a highlight [2]. It peaks in the 1850s, in 43 of 864 paintings, twice its average rate, and favors Dutch marine painters: Pieter Gerardus van Os carries it in 4 of 13 dated works, Willem van de Velde the Elder in 3 of 14 [2]. Iranian paintings carry it seven times the archive's base rate [2]. It shares canvases with [[cream]] and [[beige]] far more than chance alone predicts [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[2].
